scalars.scalar_value: Experience in performing veterinarian-directed rehabilitation on horses, including the use of an underwater treadmill, equicizer, controlled lunging, equi-therapy bands, etc.
Extensive experience handling, catching, restraining horses of all ages, sexes and behaviors, as well as training experience in introducing horses to new environments and activities.

items.item_text: Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program
Extensive experience handling, catching, restraining horses of all ages, sexes and behaviors, as well as training experience in introducing horses to new environments and activities.
Experience in performing veterinarian-directed rehabilitation on horses, including the use of an underwater treadmill, equicizer, controlled lunging, equi-therapy bands, etc.
Experience safely driving truck and horse trailer.
Skill in both physical and chemical restraint methods for equids, including the use of nose twitch, restraint stocks, breeding hobbles, and experience working with sedated horses.
Previous experience in a clinical sports medicine program or high-performance training setting is desired.

Under general supervision, provide animal health technician support to the following programmatic areas: the UC Davis Equine Rehabilitation and Layup programs, the Contagious Equine Metritis (CEM) Quarantine program and the Center for Equine Health (CEH) teaching and research herd.

Skills to communicate clearly, effectively and professionally both orally and in writing, including the ability to interpret and understand discharge instructions, department and university practices and operating procedures, manuals, safety regulations, directives and other work-related communications.
Computer skills to maintain electronic medical records, email daily updates, manage electronic calendars, etc.

Ability to recognize sick and/or injured horses, check vital signs, perform daily medical treatments, draw blood, give injections, bandage limbs and wounds, administer prescribed medications and other technical tasks.
